item.title: Ep 1 · Ch 1 — Emotion as the Prime Mover of Change
item.description:
Chapter 1: Introduction: The Nature of EFT
Why EFT treats emotion not as a symptom to manage but as the mechanism of change itself, with isolation and insecure bonding as the underlying danger. Listeners learn the process pivot from argument content to emotional process, and how to validate secondary reactivity while reaching for the primary fear and longing beneath it.

item.title: Ep 2 · Ch 1 — Secure Dependency: Working Within and Between
item.description:
Chapter 1: Introduction: The Nature of EFT
A synthesis of EFT's three stages -- de-escalation, restructuring, consolidation -- around the goal of fostering secure dependency. Listeners get the golden thread of linking inner emotional reality to the interactional cycle, plus concrete moves for tracking the dance and resisting the pull toward skill-building.

item.title: Ep 3 · Ch 1 — From Angry Protest to a Vulnerable Reach
item.description:
Chapter 1: Introduction: The Nature of EFT
A blow-by-blow breakdown of a prototypical EFT change event, where one partner's desperate anger masks a cry for connection and the other's withdrawal defends against feeling like a failure. Listeners learn to catch the bullet, cook the primary emotion, and choreograph the enactment without moving too soon.

item.title: Ep 4 · Ch 1 — When EFT Must Stop: Abuse, Addiction, Suppression
item.description:
Chapter 1: Introduction: The Nature of EFT
Contraindications and hard emotional blocks -- ongoing violence, unacknowledged active addiction, and clients too flooded to access any primary emotion. Listeners learn how to assess safety, set boundaries before deep emotional work, and normalize suppression as a costly but brilliant survival strategy.

item.title: Ep 5 · Ch 1 — Skill-Teaching and Rescuing: The Therapist's Two Survival Moves
item.description:
Chapter 1: Introduction: The Nature of EFT
How the clinician's own models of self and other shape what happens when the room escalates -- avoidant therapists reaching for communication skills, anxious therapists rushing to rescue. Listeners learn to regulate their own cycle first and hold empathy for both survival strategies rather than picking sides.

item.title: Ep 6 · Ch 2 — Hardwired for Connection: Attachment as EFT's Bedrock
item.description:
Chapter 2: Theoretical Background to EFT
Walks through attachment theory's core tenets — cradle-to-grave proximity seeking, separation distress, and the A.R.E. question (Accessible, Responsive, Engaged) — and shows how they reframe symptoms from pathology to survival strategy. Listeners learn to read anxious pursuit as protest and avoidant distancing as protection, then use the EFT Tango to move a couple below secondary anger into primary fear.

item.title: Ep 7 · Ch 2 — Tracking the Cycle Instead of Debating the Content
item.description:
Chapter 2: Theoretical Background to EFT
A practical synthesis of how to spot hyperactivating versus deactivating regulation strategies in the first minutes of a session and map the demand-withdraw loop as circular causality. Includes the red flags that you've been pulled into content, the process-reflection move that stops the content train, and a week of drills for cycle mapping and validation.

item.title: Ep 8 · Ch 2 — The Party Fight: When the Man Is the Pursuer
item.description:
Chapter 2: Theoretical Background to EFT
Deconstructs the chapter's session transcripts, where the husband pursues for closeness and the wife withdraws feeling like a disappointment — overturning the assumption that women pursue and men withdraw. Tracks the couple from the reactive Session 1 surface to the Session 10 enactment where each names the primary fear underneath.

item.title: Ep 9 · Ch 2 — Secondary Armor and the Fearful-Avoidant Whiplash
item.description:
Chapter 2: Theoretical Background to EFT
How to metabolize the rage, contempt, and dissociation that blow therapists off course, and how to recognize fearful-avoidant (disorganized) attachment when a client demands connection then violently rejects it. Teaches pacing — slicing it thinner instead of pushing an enactment — and honoring the defense rather than dismantling it.

item.title: Ep 10 · Ch 2 — Anchor in the Storm: The Therapist's Own Attachment
item.description:
Chapter 2: Theoretical Background to EFT
Examines how the therapist's own attachment style leaks into the room — colluding with the pursuer, or intellectualizing to escape the withdrawer's flatness — and how the therapist gets absorbed into the couple's cycle. Offers the internal pivot, transparency scripts, and the down-regulation stance that makes therapeutic presence itself the intervention.

item.title: Ep 11 · Ch 3 — The TEA Framework and Emotion's Four-Step Sequence
item.description:
Chapter 3: EFT Interventions
Lays out EFT's three tasks — therapeutic alliance, engaging emotion, and shaping affiliative interactions — and the difference between reactive secondary emotion and core primary emotion. Walks emotion as a process: perception, bodily arousal, meaning making, and the action tendency that organizes behavior around attachment needs.

item.description:
Chapter 3: EFT Interventions
A working playbook for Task 2: empathic reflection, validation, evocative responding, heightening, and empathic conjecture. Shows how to move a client from accepting reactive emotion to touching core vulnerability without tripping cognitive defenses.

item.description:
Chapter 3: EFT Interventions
Breaks down Task 3 — restructuring interactions — using the SHAPE sequence for staging enactments and the five moves of the EFT Tango, illustrated through the case of Jade and Beau. Includes how to slice the risk thinner when a client can't yet turn and speak.

item.title: Ep 14 · Ch 3 — Catching Bullets and Turning Disquisitions Into Doorways
item.description:
Chapter 3: EFT Interventions
How to intercept a hostile remark, reframe it with an empathic conjecture before the partner defends, and contain escalating aggression in the room. Covers tracking and reflecting the interaction pattern, framing the pattern as the shared enemy, and using disquisitions as a back door into blocked emotion.

item.title: Ep 15 · Ch 3 — ARE Presence, RISSSC, and Repairing Alliance Ruptures
item.description:
Chapter 3: EFT Interventions
Unpacks Task 1: building the alliance through accessibility, responsiveness, and emotional engagement, plus attunement, acceptance, genuineness, and therapist transparency. Teaches RISSSC — repeat, images, simple, slow, soft, client's words — as the delivery style that deepens emotion, and how to catch and repair ruptures mid-session.

item.title: Ep 16 · Ch 4 — Building a Safe Haven While Mapping the Cycle
item.description:
Chapter 4: Stage 1: Alliance, Assessment, and Cycles
How EFT's first two steps work: becoming the secure base for both partners while tracking the negative interactional cycle of secondary reactions that masks primary attachment fears. Covers empathic attunement, tracking the within-and-between sequence, and framing the cycle as the couple's shared enemy rather than each other.

item.title: Ep 17 · Ch 4 — Joining, Validating, Reframing: A Stage One Playbook
item.description:
Chapter 4: Stage 1: Alliance, Assessment, and Cycles
A practical sequence for the assessment session: join and attune, reflect the within and the between, dual-validate both partners' survival moves, then reframe character flaws as attachment longings. Includes the internal monologue that keeps you out of the content debate and off either partner's side.

item.title: Ep 18 · Ch 4 — Inez and Fernando: Anatomy of One Couple's Dance
item.description:
Chapter 4: Stage 1: Alliance, Assessment, and Cycles
A step-by-step dissection of a real cycle — Fernando feels crowded and snaps, Inez hears 'he hates me' and puffs up, Fernando retreats to his computer, Inez is left alone. Shows how the therapist slows the argument down, reflects the sighs and tears, and reframes her anger as a long attempt to reach him.

item.description:
Chapter 4: Stage 1: Alliance, Assessment, and Cycles
How to intercept a hostile comment before it lands — translating aggression into the pain underneath — plus reflecting incongruence between words and body, and validating one partner without invalidating the other. Includes what to do when a client argues with your validation.

item.title: Ep 20 · Ch 4 — Genuineness, Repair, and the Personal Question
item.description:
Chapter 4: Stage 1: Alliance, Assessment, and Cycles
What to do when a client challenges your competence or asks whether you fight with your own spouse. Being an undefended human in the room — owning errors cleanly, answering the fear behind the question — gives insecurely attached clients a disconfirming experience of rupture and repair.

item.title: Ep 21 · Ch 5 — Making the Cycle the Enemy, Not Your Partner
item.description:
Chapter 5: Stage 1: De-escalation and Stabilization
Learn how Steps 3 and 4 of Stage 1 move a couple from fighting over chores to seeing their negative pattern as the shared threat, by reading secondary emotions like nagging or stonewalling as protests of loss and bids for protection. Covers assembling primary affect with RISSSC and the reframes that unite partners against the dance.

item.description:
Chapter 5: Stage 1: De-escalation and Stabilization
A practical playbook for validation, evocative responding, heightening, empathic conjecture, and reframing, plus how to track an interaction from trigger through perception, body, meaning, and action tendency. Includes what to do when the listening partner rolls their eyes or dismisses the vulnerability you just accessed.

item.title: Ep 23 · Ch 5 — Ingrid and Frances: Staging a Reach Underneath the Hate
item.description:
Chapter 5: Stage 1: De-escalation and Stabilization
A move-by-move breakdown of a volatile pursue-withdraw session, including Frances laughing while calling herself useless and Ingrid answering her partner's shame with 'I don't trust her.' Shows how the therapist processes the rejection, blocks the exit, and sets up an enactment underneath the hate.

item.title: Ep 24 · Ch 5 — The Deceptive Calm of Withdraw-Withdraw Couples
item.description:
Chapter 5: Stage 1: De-escalation and Stabilization
How to spot couples who never fight but are quietly starving, including the burnt-out pursuer who simply gave up, and why we don't really fight should set off alarm bells. Learn to validate avoidance as protection, then thaw the freeze without triggering panic.

item.title: Ep 25 · Ch 5 — Siding With the Reasonable One: Stage One Therapist Traps
item.description:
Chapter 5: Stage 1: De-escalation and Stabilization
Self-of-the-therapist work for Stage 1: recognizing when the couple's pattern pulls you into siding with the reasonable pursuer, intellectualizing to flee conflict, or rushing to fix pain instead of staying in it. Offers grounding moves and re-centering scripts for holding volatile emotion without getting burned.

item.title: Ep 26 · Ch 6 — Eight Themes That Move a Withdrawer Into Vulnerability
item.description:
Chapter 6: Stage 2: Withdrawer Re-engagement
Walks the sequence that takes a shut-down partner from imagining disclosure to voicing an attachment need, and explains why avoidance is a defense against feeling inadequate rather than indifference. Listeners learn where the withdrawer's recoil shows up and how the therapist lingers there instead of pushing past it.

item.title: Ep 27 · Ch 6 — The Enactment Drip: Stretching the Window of Tolerance
item.description:
Chapter 6: Stage 2: Withdrawer Re-engagement
A practical synthesis of how iterative, small-risk enactments (not one dramatic confession) re-engage a withdrawer, including the somatic markers that signal a retreat into cognition. Covers the two red flags to catch: the 'summary' enactment and the listening partner's reactive skepticism.

A close reading of the Jon and Rosalita transcript, tracking how the therapist turns a physical sensation in Jon's chest into the anchor for three successively deeper enactments. Shows how the pivot to Rosalita frames his risk as strength and produces the bonding moment.

item.description:
Chapter 6: Stage 2: Withdrawer Re-engagement
How to handle the two ways a withdrawer enactment breaks down: the withdrawer's numb 'I don't know,' and the pursuing partner attacking the new vulnerability. Teaches slicing the emotional risk thinner and containing secondary anger before it crushes the reach.

Examines how the clinician's own dread of making things worse leads them to rescue clients from the emotional depth Stage 2 requires, mirroring the withdrawer's avoidance. Offers grounding and transparency moves for staying regulated while a client sits in pain.

item.description:
Chapter 7: Stage 2: Softening
Blamer softening is the Stage 2 change event where the pursuing partner moves from secondary reactive anger to the primary attachment fear underneath and asks for comfort from vulnerability. Listeners learn how the EFT Tango sequences this shift, and why reaching for insight instead of expanding the emotion short-circuits it.

item.description:
Chapter 7: Stage 2: Softening
A practical map of Bradley and Furrow's six shifts, from choreographing a possible reach through processing the fear of reaching, view of self, view of other, the actual enactment, and the withdrawer's response. Includes the markers that signal a blamer is ready to soften and the RISSSC pacing and proxy-voice phrasing that hold them there.

item.title: Ep 34 · Ch 7 — Heightening the Fear of Reaching, Not Bypassing It
item.description:
Chapter 7: Stage 2: Softening
Most failed softenings come from staging the enactment before the blamer's terror of reaching has been fully processed, producing a flat, cognitive request. Listeners learn to distinguish view-of-self blocks from view-of-other blocks, tailor empathic conjectures accordingly, and hold back a partner's premature reassurance.

item.title: Ep 35 · Ch 7 — The Rescuer Trap and the Unlovable Self
item.description:
Chapter 7: Stage 2: Softening
When a client's self-shame turns unbearable, the therapist's impulse to comfort or reassure usurps the partner's role and invalidates the pain. This episode covers managing that countertransference, staying with profound negative views of self rooted in early trauma, and channeling historical pain into an enactment with the partner.

item.title: Ep 36 · Ch 8 — Consolidating Security Through a New Relational Narrative
item.description:
Chapter 8: Stage 3: Consolidation and Common EFT Impasses
Why Stage 3 is active work rather than a victory lap: the therapist highlights the contrast between the old cycle and the new one, guides the couple to author a shared story of their change, and builds attachment rituals that sustain the bond outside the room. Listeners learn why a fight in Stage 3 is an opportunity for repair, not evidence of failure.

item.description:
Chapter 8: Stage 3: Consolidation and Common EFT Impasses
A practical playbook for Steps 8 and 9 — revisiting old pragmatic problems (money, chores, parenting) inside the new secure frame, and validating the couple's new moves rather than problem-solving content. Includes how to spot pseudo-consolidation, where a couple stops fighting to avoid the work instead of genuinely repairing the bond.

item.description:

Listeners see how the therapist tracks Inez's spontaneous move to protect Fernando, holds his shame without rescuing him, and bridges emotional safety to physical intimacy instead of drifting into sex-therapy content.

Listeners see how the therapist tracks Inez's spontaneous move to protect Fernando, holds his shame without rescuing him, and bridges emotional safety to physical intimacy instead of drifting into sex-therapy content.

item.title: Ep 39 · Ch 8 — Slicing It Thinner When the Process Stalls
item.description:
Chapter 8: Stage 3: Consolidation and Common EFT Impasses
How to read an impasse as a system defending itself rather than a resistant client: name the stuckness transparently, lower the emotional risk of an enactment until it is small enough to take, and source the block in attachment history. Also covers the disquisition technique and the red flag of retreating into cognitive problem-solving.

item.title: Ep 40 · Ch 8 — Owning the Miss: Repairing Ruptures With Clients
item.description:
Chapter 8: Stage 3: Consolidation and Common EFT Impasses
What to do when a client turns on the therapist and the alliance breaks — take radical responsibility, apologize authentically, and ask the client directly how you should intervene next time. Listeners learn why an apology strengthens rather than undermines clinical authority, and when an individual session is the right repair tool.

item.title: Ep 41 · Ch 9 — The Protective Prison: Reading Symptoms as Attachment Strategies
item.description:
Chapter 9: Emotionally Focused Individual Therapy (EFIT)
How EFIT reframes depression, anxiety, and trauma symptoms as protective strategies against a core attachment threat rather than individual pathology. Covers the within-between cycle, the ARE therapist stance, and affect assembly down to the primary emotion.

item.title: Ep 42 · Ch 9 — Running the EFT Tango With an Individual Client
item.description:
Chapter 9: Emotionally Focused Individual Therapy (EFIT)
A step-by-step walkthrough of the five Tango moves adapted for individual therapy, from mirroring present process to shaping an internal encounter between parts of the self. Includes how to spot emotional handles, interrupt storytelling, and distill affect instead of problem-solving.

item.title: Ep 43 · Ch 9 — May's Heavy Balloon: From Numbing to Naked Terror
item.description:
Chapter 9: Emotionally Focused Individual Therapy (EFIT)
A session-by-session analysis of May, a depressed client who deflects with 'I'm fine really,' showing how the therapist uses RISSSC and affect assembly to reach the terror of being alone. Ends with an enactment where May's adult self speaks to her frozen ten-year-old self.

item.title: Ep 44 · Ch 9 — Catching the Spin When Clients Intellectualize and Numb
item.description:
Chapter 9: Emotionally Focused Individual Therapy (EFIT)
What to do when there is no partner in the room and the client's self-protective spin stalls the work: notice the avoidance marker, validate its survival function, and pivot back to the body. Covers the content trap, kind interruptions, and reframing symptoms as protection.

item.description:
Chapter 9: Emotionally Focused Individual Therapy (EFIT)
Why the alliance in EFIT is the intervention, and how the therapist's own triggered attachment anxieties (the blank slate, the savior complex) compromise it. Shows how to use countertransference openly to model secure attachment and offer effective dependency.

item.title: Ep 46 · Ch 10 — The CARE Model: From Diagnosis to an Attachment Lens on Trauma
item.description:
Chapter 10: Healing the Echoes of Trauma Through EFIT
How interpersonal trauma warps working models of self and other, and why numbing, hypervigilance, and self-loathing are best read as functional survival strategies rather than pathology. Introduces the CARE model (Context, Attachment, Relationship, Emotion) as the shift from a diagnostic to an attachment lens.

item.title: Ep 47 · Ch 10 — Pacing Affect Assembly Inside the Window of Tolerance
item.description:
Chapter 10: Healing the Echoes of Trauma Through EFIT
The Stage 1 EFIT playbook for trauma survivors: using Tango Move 1 to mirror present process, knowing when to contain versus heighten emotion, and using Move 2 to assemble the five elements of emotion (trigger, perception, body, meaning, action tendency). Includes grounding language for the moment a client starts to dissociate.

item.title: Ep 48 · Ch 10 — Sandy and Her Younger Self: Staging the Encounter
item.description:
Chapter 10: Healing the Echoes of Trauma Through EFIT
A session-by-session breakdown of Sandy, a client with developmental trauma and suicidal ideation, as the therapist stages a Tango Move 3 encounter between her adult self and the frozen younger self behind the bedroom door. Shows why traumatized parts reject flimsy reassurance and how honest, grounded presence builds trust inside the self-system.

item.title: Ep 49 · Ch 10 — Taming Shame and Meeting Mistrust Without Getting Defensive
item.description:
Chapter 10: Healing the Echoes of Trauma Through EFIT
How to handle the roadblocks of trauma work: framing self-blame as a child's bid for control rather than trying to argue a client out of shame, containing emotion when a client floods, and hearing "this isn't working" as an attachment test rather than a verdict on your competence.

item.title: Ep 50 · Ch 10 — Staying the Stronger, Wiser Other Under Protest
item.description:
Chapter 10: Healing the Echoes of Trauma Through EFIT
What to do with your own nervous system when a client's anger, accusation, or sudden suicidal threat knocks you off balance. Covers de-personalizing protest, noticing when your own attachment strategy gets triggered, and staying humanly attuned even while managing risk.

item.title: Ep 51 · Ch 11 — The Wall Between Them: When Trauma Blocks the Safe Haven
item.description:
Chapter 11: Facing Trauma Together Through EFT
How trauma restricts the window of tolerance and turns once-adaptive coping strategies — numbing, dissociation, withdrawal — into barriers that block a couple from using each other as a safe haven. Introduces attachment injuries as specific relational traumas and shows how the therapist normalizes the wall, works the bodily felt sense, and choreographs an enactment of fear and need.

item.title: Ep 52 · Ch 11 — The Attachment Injury Resolution Model, Step by Step
item.description:
Chapter 11: Facing Trauma Together Through EFT
Walks the four AIRM steps — articulating the impact, differentiating the affect, re-engagement and ownership, forgiveness and reconciliation — and why the focus must shift from the facts of the betrayal to its attachment meaning. Includes how to block the offending partner's shame spiral so their remorse can actually land on the injured partner's fear.

item.title: Ep 53 · Ch 11 — Randy and Karen: Grief, Betrayal, and Unedited Remorse
item.description:
Chapter 11: Facing Trauma Together Through EFT
Follows a 30-year couple through Randy's childhood trauma, his numbing and infidelity, and Karen's guarded self-protection, tracing how the therapist grounds Randy when toxic shame hijacks his empathy and he goes blank. Shows the vacillation reflection, the body-barometer question, and what a genuinely unedited apology sounds like when it lands.

item.title: Ep 54 · Ch 11 — Blank-Outs, Shame Spirals, and Honoring the Armor
item.description:
Chapter 11: Facing Trauma Together Through EFT
Practical moves for the three most common stuck points in trauma and injury work: grounding a dissociating client, interrupting a shame collapse without letting the offender off the hook, and validating an injured partner's refusal to trust an apology. Covers flooding markers and why you never push an enactment on a flooded client.

item.title: Ep 55 · Ch 11 — Witnessing the Couple's Pain Without Carrying It
item.description:
Chapter 11: Facing Trauma Together Through EFT
Examines how the therapist's own attachment fears — the urge to rescue, to fix, to judge the offending partner — crack the therapeutic container and confirm the couple's belief that their pain is too much to be held. Offers internal grounding scripts, pacing pauses, and the distinction between carrying a couple's pain and witnessing it.

item.title: Ep 56 · Ch 12 — The Vertical Bond: EFFT Versus Couples Work
item.description:
Chapter 12: Emotionally Focused Family Therapy
Why EFFT targets the caregiver-child bond rather than the reciprocal partner bond, and how a child's defiance or withdrawal reads as an attachment strategy aimed at an inaccessible parent. Covers running the EFT Tango with families, and why the child is never asked to be the parent's emotional caretaker.

item.title: Ep 57 · Ch 12 — Stabilize the Parent Before Restructuring the Child
item.description:
Chapter 12: Emotionally Focused Family Therapy
A step-by-step clinical sequence from Stage 1 de-escalation to Stage 2 restructuring: track the family cycle, process parental blocks first, then access the child's primary attachment emotion and choreograph the caregiving enactment. Includes red flags for when a parent starts lecturing mid-enactment.

item.title: Ep 58 · Ch 12 — Distilling an Adolescent's Anger Into Her Longing
item.description:
Chapter 12: Emotionally Focused Family Therapy
A session-level walkthrough of Fatemah and her daughter Abeer, showing how the therapist heightens Abeer's hurt beneath her defiance and sets up her reach: 'your opinion is the one that matters most.' Demonstrates how to help a parent receive that bid with comfort instead of correction.

item.title: Ep 59 · Ch 12 — Finding the Panic Beneath Parental Criticism
item.description:
Chapter 12: Emotionally Focused Family Therapy
How to identify and dismantle relational blocks in parents who either over-respond with criticism or under-respond with helplessness, by validating caregiving intent and moving them from reactive defense into fear, grief, or shame. Also addresses the countertransference trap of siding with the child.

item.description:
